# QEMU (static, from source)

This directory builds the QEMU tarball pinned by the `@qemu_linux_x86_64` Bazel
repository (`bazel/module/qemu_repositories.bzl`, pin in `version.bzl`) for the
test VMs, so neither CI nor developer machines need a QEMU package, and one QEMU
build runs everywhere: a saved VM state only resumes on the QEMU build and
machine type it was saved with.

## What Is Built

- QEMU 11.1.1, `qemu-system-x86_64` (KVM only, no TCG) and `qemu-img`,
  fully static against musl (static-pie, no interpreter), with user networking
  (libslirp), zstd (the test images are zstd-compressed qcow2) and vvfat (the
  image build passes Windows Setup its answer file on a virtual FAT floppy), no
  GUI or VNC.
- Every linked library is built from a pinned source (`sources.txt`): glib, pcre2,
  pixman, libslirp, zlib, zstd. glib's build also needs libffi, which is not
  linked. Alpine 3.22 (the builder image) provides only the toolchain; musl's
  `libc.a` and gcc's `libgcc.a`/`libatomic.a` end up in the binaries.
- Only the firmware the test VMs load (`share/qemu/`): SeaBIOS, the std VGA BIOS,
  the e1000 option ROM, kvmvapic, enough for the i440fx machine (`pc`) with an
  e1000 NIC; q35 or another NIC fails at start for want of its ROM. The
  binaries are built for a prefix that does not exist on any host
  (`/nonexistent-qemu`), so they find `share/qemu` next to `bin/` (or through
  `-L`) and never pick up a system QEMU's firmware.
- `BUILDINFO` records the configure flags, the linked archives of both binaries,
  the sources, the builder image (`builder-image.txt`), the toolchain packages and
  the sha256 of every file.

The recipe is modelled on hermeticbuild/qemu-prebuilt (MIT), which has no zstd.

## Building and Publishing

`create-archive` runs inside the builder image pinned in `builder-image.txt` and
writes `qemu-<version>-<revision>-linux-x86_64.tar.xz` and `sources/` to the current
directory. It fetches each source from the Nexus mirror first, then from upstream,
and checks it against `sources.txt`. Locally (pulling from Harbor needs a
`docker login int-registry.lan.checkmk.net`):

```
mkdir -p out
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/third_party/qemu:/recipe:ro" \
    -v "$PWD/out:/out" -w /out "$(cat third_party/qemu/builder-image.txt)" bash /recipe/create-archive
```

The build is reproducible (fixed build path, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` from the QEMU
tarball, sorted tar with fixed owners), so a new version is pinned from a local
build. In one commit, bump:

- `sources.txt` (it names every version),
- the archive name and sha256 in `version.bzl`,
- `REVISION` in `create-archive` when the archive changes for the same QEMU
  version: published names are never reused, so older pins keep resolving.

Then run the manual Jenkins job `build-qemu-from-source`
(`buildscripts/scripts/build_qemu.sh`). It rebuilds the archive, refuses one that
does not match `version.bzl`, and publishes whatever of it and its sources the
mirror lacks. As every run rebuilds, a run also checks that the recipe still
reproduces the pin.

The libslirp tarball is generated by GitLab, which does not keep it byte-stable.
When bumping it, upload the copy whose sha256 went into `sources.txt` to
upstream-archives yourself, before running the job: otherwise the job fetches it
from GitLab again and fails if the bytes changed in between.

## The Builder Image

The build runs in the image named, with its digest, in `builder-image.txt`
(Harbor project `ci-qemu`; Nexus deletes docker images nobody pulls for 30 days,
and this one is pulled only when QEMU is rebuilt), so a local build and the job's
build use the same toolchain. `Dockerfile` builds it from an Alpine base pinned by
digest in the same project; its packages are whatever Alpine has at the time.

To change the toolchain, run the manual Jenkins job
`buildscripts/scripts/build-qemu-builder-image.groovy`: it builds the image with
kaniko, pushes it under a new tag and prints the reference to put in
`builder-image.txt`. A new image changes the archive (at least the toolchain
packages in `BUILDINFO`), so the same commit bumps `REVISION` and re-pins
`version.bzl` from a build in the new image.

Its tags read `<date>-<blob>-b<build number>`: the day it was built, the git
blob of the `Dockerfile` it was built from, and the job's build number. The
`Dockerfile` copies nothing in, so it is the image's whole recipe; its blob,
unlike a commit, survives rebases and the merge. Alpine's packages change over
time, so two builds of the same `Dockerfile` can differ: the date and build
number tell them apart. The commit that introduced that `Dockerfile` (and the
one that replaced it, if any):

```
git log --find-object=<blob> -- third_party/qemu/Dockerfile
```

## Licence

QEMU is GPL-2.0-only; SeaBIOS LGPL-3.0, iPXE GPL-2.0-or-later, glib
LGPL-2.1-or-later, pcre2 BSD-3-Clause (with the PCRE2 exception), pixman MIT,
libslirp BSD-3-Clause and MIT, zlib Zlib, zstd BSD-3-Clause or GPL-2.0, musl MIT.
The tarball carries every licence under `LICENSES/`. The sources of QEMU, its
firmware and every library built here (the tarballs in `sources.txt`, this recipe)
are published next to it. musl's `libc.a` and gcc's `libgcc.a`/`libatomic.a` come
from the builder image's Alpine packages; the musl tarball is there for its
licence.
